seo.title: EnerMod Africa: the African Energy Modelling Observatory
seo.description: An open observatory of energy modelling studies and tools applied to African countries, kept up to date by contributions and regular literature searches. Curators check every addition.

common.tagline: An open inventory of energy modelling studies on African countries, kept up to date by curators and contributors.
common.beta: Beta: data and features are evolving

footer.institutions: An AISESA Cluster 1 activity. The initial review and the first version of the platform were produced at the Centre de Mathématiques Appliquées of MINES Paris-PSL (The Transition Institute 1.5).

home.title: Who models Africa’s energy future?
home.lede: An open observatory of energy modelling studies on African countries, the tools they use and the institutions that lead them. It started with a systematic review and is kept up to date by curators and contributors.
home.trust: Every study individually verified · every score documented · every figure updates as the inventory grows.

home.questionsTitle: Built to answer questions such as

questions.q1: Which countries are heavily modelled, and which are barely studied at all?
questions.q2: Which tools dominate, and are they open, or locked behind licences?
questions.q3: How much of this research is led by African institutions?
questions.q4: Do the models capture what shapes African energy systems: informal economies, charcoal and biomass, unreliable supply, rapid urbanisation?
questions.q5: Which countries have the institutions and data to put models to work?

home.originLede: Author institutions by country, counted once per study. African researchers now lead the majority of the record, but leadership thins where the stakes are highest: whole energy-system planning.
home.originCaption: Two colour ramps: African institutions in green, institutions outside Africa in brown. Hover a country for its count.
home.scopeText: Studies are grouped by the scope of the model they use; statistics mixing the two can mislead, so every analytical page filters by scope.
home.fullText: Long-term planning models: MESSAGE, OSeMOSYS, TIMES, LEAP, PLEXOS, Balmorel. All 51 fields extracted.
home.lightText: Techno-economic, GIS, mini-grid, electrification and calculators: HOMER, OnSSET, RETScreen. Core fields only.
home.latestText: Studies that entered the inventory most recently, through the review, contributions or discovery.
home.storyLede: Six pages, one question. Start with the map and end with the methodology that makes every number auditable.

home.partnersText: EnerMod Africa carries out Activity 1 of AISESA Cluster 1 (clean energy pathways for sustainable development): mapping the energy modelling tools and analytical capacities that already exist across the continent. The initial review and the first version of the platform were produced at MINES Paris-PSL (The Transition Institute 1.5).

gaps.title: What the models leave out
gaps.lede: African energy systems have features that many global models were not built to capture: large informal economies, charcoal and biomass, unreliable supply, rapid urbanisation. This page shows how often the studies take them into account.
gaps.scopeHelp: Focused models leave methodological fields empty because those fields do not apply to them, not because less effort went into extraction.
gaps.scopeAllHelp: Statistics aggregate whole energy-system and focused models together, which can be misleading.
gaps.regionHint: Applies to the maps and the table, not to the headline coverage figures.
gaps.featuresLede: Share of the {n, number} studies in scope that address each feature, counted only where the study was assessed on it.
gaps.featuresCaption: The dashed line is the median across the four features.
gaps.whoLede: African-led: the first author, or all authors, are at African institutions. Mixed: a non-African first author in a team with African institutions. Non-African: all authors outside Africa.
gaps.whoCaption: {n, number} studies with a stated affiliation.
gaps.whereCaption: Author institutions by country, counted once per study, for the {n, number} studies in the current scope and region.
gaps.gapMapLede: The gap score combines coverage of African specificities, data availability, energy governance and model density. Higher means more under-served.
gaps.gapTableCaption: The 15 highest-gap countries in the selected regions.
gaps.financeTitle: Do the models account for how projects are financed?
gaps.financeLede: Capital cost and financing assumptions shape every investment result, yet are often left implicit or uniform.
gaps.modeRateHint: used by {share}% of the {n, number} studies that state one
gaps.variedHint: range or scenario-specific cost of capital
gaps.unstatedHint: {m} studies name a specific financing mechanism
gaps.rateCaption: Base-case discount rate stated by the studies. Most assume a uniform rate despite wide differences in real financing costs across African countries.
gaps.emergingLede: Tracked from the start; the counts rise as grey literature and policy documents are integrated.
gaps.method: Every score on this page is documented, with its formula and sources, on the
gaps.gapMapCaption: Five fixed classes, so the map compares over time. Select a country to open its page.

readiness.title: Country readiness to use models
readiness.lede: Readiness combines institutional capacity, data availability, climate commitments and electrification: the conditions a country needs to run, maintain and use models for policy.
readiness.headline: {n} countries score below 4/10. Readiness gaps concentrate less around electrification and more around governance frameworks and data transparency.
readiness.mapCaption: {n} countries without RISE coverage, mostly small island states, are not ranked rather than scored as unready.
readiness.scatterTitle: Where modelling gaps meet institutional readiness
readiness.caveat: Energy governance is a declared proxy: RISE measures the regulatory framework, not modelling capacity. Formulas and sources are on the
readiness.scatterLede: One panel per region, the other regions in grey. The three highest-gap countries of each panel carry their ISO3 code.
readiness.mapLede: Readiness 0–10 in five fixed classes. Select a country to open its page.

recommender.title: Choosing a modelling tool
recommender.lede: Answer six questions on your objective, scale, budget, team, time horizon and data, and add other requirements if needed. The recommender then ranks the publicly available tools in the inventory.
recommender.weightsHint: A transparent heuristic to shortlist candidates, not a verdict.
recommender.openOnly: Only the {n} open-source tools are ranked, as requested.
recommender.internalNote: {n} in-house models that are not publicly available are listed in the inventory but never ranked.
recommender.disclaimer: The score adds transparent points per criterion; it does not replace expert judgement, a pilot or a conversation with the tool's community. Use the assistant below to ask why a tool ranked where it did.
recommender.allToolsLede: Browse the full inventory with its licences, learning curves and track records.

q.allowedHint: The scales and horizons offered follow the objective chosen in question 1.

objective.national_planning: National energy planning (supply mix, capacity expansion)
objective.electrification: Electrification and energy access planning (grid extension, off-grid, geospatial least-cost)
objective.prefeasibility: Project or site pre-feasibility (mini-grid, hybrid system, plant design)
objective.operation: Power system operation, dispatch and reliability
objective.emissions: Emissions, air quality and climate impact assessment

budget.none: No budget (free tools, including free licences for African institutions)

extras.non_windows: Team works on macOS or Linux

contribute.title: Contribute to the inventory
contribute.lede: Propose a missing study, correct a record or describe a tool. A curator verifies every proposal before it is published.
contribute.studyIntro: Minimum: the title, the tools used and the countries modelled. Everything else helps the curator and can be completed later from the publication.
contribute.correctionIntro: Tell us what is wrong and what it should be. Refer to a study number or a tool name when you can.
contribute.toolIntro: A tool that is missing from the inventory, or a profile to update. Repository and website links let the tracker follow it.

f.title: Title of the study
f.doiHint: A DOI lets us check for duplicates and fetch metadata.
f.countriesHint: Hold Ctrl or Cmd to select several.
f.name: Your name

contribute.youHint: Optional, but an e-mail lets the curator come back to you. Sign in to follow your contributions.
contribute.consent: By submitting you agree that the proposal (not your contact details) may be published in the inventory under CC BY 4.0 once verified.
contribute.thanksText: Your proposal is in the curation queue. It will appear in the observatory once a curator has verified it.
contribute.duplicate: It looks similar to an existing record, which the curator will check:

how.title: How it works
how.s1: You submit a proposal; duplicates are flagged automatically.
how.s2: A curator verifies it against the publication, completes the fields and approves or declines it.
how.s3: Approved studies enter the inventory with their source marked as a contribution.

criteria.title: What belongs in the inventory
criteria.c1: A named energy modelling tool, or ad hoc GIS analysis or system dynamics, applied to a community or territorial energy system.
criteria.c3: Peer-reviewed articles, theses, reports and proceedings in English or French.
criteria.c4: Not: single private facilities modelling their own supply; purely top-down macroeconomic models.
